skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: +4 unit, headless unchanged at 245: THE CAPTURE HARNESS NOW REFUSES A VACUOUS IMAGE, and the row's own stated mechanism was corrected by measurement. The harness whose whole job is to be non-vacuous printed CAPTURE PASS over 7,700 pixels of pure black. CcpVerify gained a CaptureCensus that counts DISTINCT COLOURS and refuses below two, naming the count, the pixel total and the colour so a reader can tell 'nothing was drawn' from 'a photograph of an empty panel'. Two design points worth keeping: 'entirely the background' needed no second rule, because an image that is entirely any one colour has exactly one distinct colour; and ALPHA is excluded from a colour's identity, so a transport that varies alpha over an unpainted buffer cannot manufacture a second colour. Fixed once where the doors route - capture.ps1 and capture-wslg.sh both gate on the same assembly before printing PASS, the --capture path runs the census before any named check, and self-test.ps1 inherits both. BOTH DIRECTIONS PROVED, which is what makes it a guard and not a tripwire: the fail direction was reproduced on real WSLg with the same probe line the board recorded, and the pass direction is a real Windows headed capture reading 228 distinct colours that then passes its named check 888/918. AND NOTHING CURRENTLY CAUGHT NOW PASSES - self-test.ps1 ran end to end with a deliberately regressed brush still tripping its own named check, so the census never preempts the named checks. THE ROW'S EXIT-CODE CAUSE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: I had written that dotnet run returns the RUNNER's code. Measured, dotnet run propagates the app's code correctly and it is the PIPE that swallows it - a built exe piped to tail also gives 0. Real observable, right prescribed fix, wrong named cause, and neither shipping script actually had the bug. THE LANE ALSO SURFACED A BIGGER DEFECT THAN ITS OWN ROW, now filed separately: the Linux app produced 836,000 identical black pixels across three display configurations INCLUDING with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1, so either the app does not render on Linux or no capture route on that machine can see what it renders - and this fix means that defect can no longer hide behind a green. CcpClient.Tests 3177 to 3181.
